title: TS-MTM: Temporal-Spectral Masked Time-Series Modeling for Forecasting

problem.claim: Long-term time-series forecasting requires modeling intricate periodic patterns, evolving spectral dynamics, and structural dependencies.

gap.claim: Conventional one-dimensional masked time-series modeling often does not explicitly resolve the structural dependencies needed for long-term forecasting.

contributions.claim: TS-MTM is a masked time-series modeling framework that pretrains in a joint temporal-spectral representation space.

The framework converts one-dimensional sequences into period-aware two-dimensional temporal-spectral representations using autocorrelation-based periodicity, then applies axial-period cross masking and structure-aware spectral magnitude masking.
A dual-domain contextual contrastive objective aligns temporal and spectral views to produce unified embeddings intended to preserve temporal-spectral coherence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluations on nine benchmark datasets.
The authors report consistent state-of-the-art performance in both in-domain and cross-domain settings.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Time-series forecasting depends on modeling periodic patterns and changing spectral dynamics.
One-dimensional masked time-series modeling may not explicitly capture structural dependencies required for long-term forecasting.
TS-MTM addresses the gap through joint temporal-spectral pretraining and period-aware two-dimensional representations.
APCM, SSMM, and a dual-domain contextual contrastive objective model cross-phase dependencies, global frequency signatures, and consistency between views.
The authors report strong results across nine datasets and both in-domain and cross-domain settings.

source_observation.claim: The framework represents one-dimensional sequences in a period-aware two-dimensional temporal-spectral space.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly restructuring data around detected periodicity may expose dependencies that are difficult to model in the original one-dimensional layout.

application.claim: For forecasting systems with strong periodic or frequency-domain structure, consider representation transformations that make those structures explicit before self-supervised pretraining.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this transformation benefits datasets without stable or meaningful periodic structure.

source_observation.claim: The method combines temporal masking, spectral masking, and contrastive alignment across domains.

interpretation.claim: Combining complementary masked views with an alignment objective may encourage representations that retain both local temporal dependencies and global spectral signatures.

application.claim: When multiple signal views capture distinct but related structure, use view-specific reconstruction objectives together with an explicit consistency objective.

exception.claim: The abstract does not report ablations showing the separate contribution of each masking mechanism or the contrastive objective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify model architecture, training details, or masking ratios.
The abstract does not provide dataset names, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not report ablations or computational costs.
